title: Bundibugyo virus disease outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo and Uganda at day 100: an ESCMID Emerging Infections Subcommittee update.

analysis.scope_and_question: The 2026 Bundibugyo virus disease (BVD) outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC) and Uganda has challenged epidemic control despite rapid expansion of response capacity. The review aims to reassess the threats identified by the ESCMID Emerging Infections Subcommittee at day 100 and identify clinical and public-health priorities.

The review underscores the need for improved contact tracing, active case-finding, and supportive care. It also notes that cross-reactive antibody responses from Ebola vaccination do not provide protection against BDBV. The ECDC assessed the infection likelihood for EU/EEA residents as very low. The review highlights the importance of maintaining essential health services and community engagement during outbreaks.

BVD typically presents as a nonspecific febrile and gastrointestinal illness, with haemorrhagic manifestations being rare at onset. The review highlights that EBOV-oriented testing may not detect BDBV, emphasizing the need for species-specific molecular testing in epidemiologically plausible scenarios. Supportive care remains the standard of management, but the availability of safe interventions varies between peripheral facilities and dedicated filovirus treatment centres. No vaccine or specific therapy has demonstrated clinical efficacy against BDBV in humans, with Ervebo and remdesivir-based regimens under evaluation.

title: Cross-neutralization of Bundibugyo virus following Ebola virus booster vaccination

analysis.research_question_and_background: The ongoing Bundibugyo virus disease (BVD) outbreak in the Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC) highlights the absence of a licensed Bundibugyo virus (BDBV) vaccine. analysis.study_design_and_population: In the EBO-BOOST trial (NCT06126822), previously EBOV-vaccinated adults received an ERVEBO booster after primary vaccination with ERVEBO (E|E, n=60) or ZABDENO/MVABEA (Zm|E, n=40).
analysis.methods: Neutralizing antibodies against EBOV and BDBV were measured at baseline, day 21 (D21) and month 6 (M6) using biologically contained EBOV-dVP30-eGFP and BDBV-dVP30-eGFP reporter viruses.
analysis.main_results: BDBV seropositivity increased from 8% at baseline to 67% at D21, declining to 34% at M6. Median NT50 titers were significantly lower for BDBV than for EBOV at D21 (40.9 vs 244.1; P<0.001) and at M6 (<20 vs 66.5; P<0.001).
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: In mixed-effects models adjusted for time since primary vaccination, BDBV responses were 65% lower than EBOV responses at D21 (GMR 0.35; 95% CI 0.26-0.48) and 50% lower at M6 (GMR 0.50; 95% CI 0.40-0.63).
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: Although protective significance and correlates of protection remain to be established, these findings support evaluation of ERVEBO in parallel with BDBV-specific vaccines.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The supplied evidence does not report limitations of the study.

The ongoing BVD outbreak in the Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC) underscores the need for a BDBV vaccine, as current EBOV vaccines may induce cross-reactive antibodies. The EBO-BOOST trial evaluated previously EBOV-vaccinated adults who received an ERVEBO booster after primary vaccination with ERVEBO or ZABDENO/MVABEA. Neutralizing antibodies against EBOV and BDBV were measured using reporter viruses at baseline, day 21, and month 6. Results showed that BDBV seropositivity increased significantly after the booster, but median NT50 titers were lower than those for EBOV. analysis.methods: A retrospective epidemiological analysis of publicly available WHO, CDC, and other credible surveillance and scientific data was conducted to characterize Ebola outbreaks by year, country, region, virus species, duration, cases, deaths, and case fatality rate (CFR). Orthoebolavirus zairense accounted for the majority of outbreaks (68.3%) and exhibited the highest median CFR (70.8%), although pairwise species comparisons were not statistically significant following post hoc testing.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: These findings underscore the need for sustained investment in EVD surveillance, preparedness, rapid outbreak response, and resilient healthcare systems across Africa, particularly in Central Africa, to strengthen prevention and control efforts and reduce outbreak-associated mortality.

title: Vaccine preparedness for the next emerging infectious disease crisis

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study addresses the need for improved vaccine preparedness against emerging infectious diseases, highlighting the importance of learning from the rapid development of vaccines for SARS-CoV-2.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The study is a commentary analyzing vaccine preparedness strategies, focusing on the lessons learned from the SARS-CoV-2 pandemic and the challenges in developing vaccines for emerging pathogens such as Bundibugyo virus.
analysis.methods: The methods involve a review of existing vaccine technologies, regulatory pathways, and funding initiatives, with an emphasis on mucosal immunity and the development of broadly protective vaccines.
analysis.main_results: The Bundibugyo virus outbreak in May 2026 in the Democratic Republic of the Congo served as a test for post-COVID-19 pandemic vaccine preparedness, and the study notes that the benefits of mRNA-based seasonal influenza vaccines compared to conventional ones remain debated, though their speed in case of a pandemic is a significant advantage.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpret that while strain-matched vaccines are currently favored for pandemic preparedness, the development of broadly protective vaccines could significantly enhance readiness for future viral threats.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings inform the importance of investing in vaccine platforms that can be rapidly deployed and the need for broader research into emerging viruses to improve future pandemic responses.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The evidence is based on a commentary and does not include direct experimental results, which limits its strength. However, the analysis is grounded in current vaccine development trends and policy decisions.

analysis.summary_en: This commentary discusses the importance of vaccine preparedness for emerging infectious diseases, emphasizing the lessons from the rapid development of SARS-CoV-2 vaccines. It highlights the potential of mucosal vaccines and the challenges in creating broadly protective ones due to antigenic variability. The study notes that the Bundibugyo virus outbreak in May 2026 in the Democratic Republic of the Congo serves as a test for post-COVID-19 pandemic readiness. While strain-matched vaccines are currently favored, the authors suggest that broadly protective vaccines could enhance preparedness for future viral threats. The analysis underscores the need for further investment in vaccine development and basic research, particularly for viruses with pandemic potential. However, the commentary lacks direct experimental results, which limits its evidence strength.

title: Implementation of Risk Communication Tabletop Exercise and Areas for Improvement: A Case Study on the Office of the Spokesperson, Korea Disease Control and Prevention Agency

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study aimed to evaluate the implementation of risk communication tabletop exercises and identify areas for improvement in the Republic of Korea, where such exercises have primarily focused on field response procedures rather than risk communication itself.
analysis.study_design_and_population: A discussion-based tabletop exercise was conducted by the Office of the Spokesperson at the Korea Disease Control and Prevention Agency, simulating escalating crisis alert levels through a spokesperson-led communication review meeting. The participants included 1 spokesperson, 7 in media communication, 6 in digital communication, 5 in communication strategy and operational support, and 2 in the red team.
analysis.methods: The exercise was developed using the World Health Organization’s Simulation Exercise Manual (2017) and involved scenarios based on Ebola virus disease and avian influenza. Participants prepared response materials by referring to manuals, standard operating procedures, and initial risk communication response procedures.
analysis.main_results: During the exercise, briefing procedures, centralized press inquiry channels, misinformation and disinformation monitoring procedures, and communication channels for external cooperation operated smoothly. However, areas where standards and roles had not been sufficiently specified showed ad hoc responses. The exercise identified improvement areas in emergency communication content, public campaigns, press communication, external cooperation implementation, and personnel and organizational operations.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpreted that systematic risk communication is necessary to earn public trust, induce voluntary compliance with prevention guidelines, and respond to misinformation and disinformation. The study presents a novel case of implementing a dedicated risk communication tabletop exercise in the Republic of Korea.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings can inform the development of evaluation frameworks for risk communication exercises, promote standardization and institutionalization of such practices, and enhance preparedness for infectious disease crises through improved communication strategies.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is limited to a single case and does not provide quantitative data on the effectiveness of the exercise. The evidence is moderate as it is based on a descriptive analysis of a tabletop exercise rather than empirical outcomes.

analysis.summary_en: This study describes the implementation of a risk communication tabletop exercise by the Korea Disease Control and Prevention Agency, highlighting the need for systematic risk communication during infectious disease crises. The exercise simulated scenarios based on Ebola virus disease and avian influenza, aiming to evaluate procedures, clarify team roles, and identify improvement areas. Key results showed that some communication processes operated smoothly, while others required ad hoc responses. The authors emphasize the importance of structured risk communication to build public trust and ensure compliance with prevention guidelines. The study identifies potential areas for enhancement in emergency communication, public campaigns, and external cooperation. However, the findings are based on a single case and lack quantitative data, limiting the strength of the evidence to moderate.

title: Managing occupational dermatitis during pandemics using virucidal emollient Dermol 500.

analysis.research_question_and_background: BackgroundWork-related contact dermatitis is a significant problem for healthcare workers. Repeated exposure to water, soap and alcohol-based gels can cause dry skin, irritation and contact dermatitis.
analysis.study_design_and_population: MethodsThe virucidal activity of Dermol 500 lotion and its antimicrobial constituents benzalkonium chloride (BAK) and chlorhexidine dihydrochloride (CD) was assessed against influenza A virus (IAV), SARS-CoV-2 and pseudotyped viruses expressing glycoproteins from 2026 outbreak strains of Ebolavirus and Hantavirus.
analysis.methods: Viruses or pseudoviruses were incubated with treatment prior to quenching serial dilution and infectivity measurement by plaque assay, tissue culture infectious dose 50 (TCID50) or bioluminescent reporter activity.
analysis.main_results: ResultsDermol 500 exhibits comparable virucidal activity to alcohol-based hand sanitisers against IAV and SARS-CoV-2. Furthermore, the Dermol 500 components BAK and CD exhibit independent and synergistic virucidal activity against IAV, SARS-CoV-2 and pseudoviruses.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: ConclusionsThe virucidal activity of Dermol 500 lotion and its active antimicrobials BAK and CD indicates its suitability as a soap substitute to treat and prevent contact dermatitis in front line workers during viral disease outbreaks.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: Teaser textOccupational dermatitis soared during the COVID-19 pandemic, but the standard treatment - the antimicrobial emollient and soap substitute Dermol 500 - was not recommended as its antiviral activity was unknown.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: Here, we address this evidence gap: Dermol 500 lotion is an effective virucide, and its constituents benzalkonium chloride (BAK) and chlorhexidine dihydrochloride (CD) effectively neutralise SARS-CoV-2, influenza A virus and pseudotyped 2026 strains of Ebolavirus and Hantavirus at concentrations 10-fold lower than the active formulation.

analysis.summary_en: This study investigates the virucidal activity of Dermol 500 lotion and its antimicrobial components, BAK and CD, against influenza A virus, SARS-CoV-2, and pseudotyped viruses from 2026 Ebolavirus and Hantavirus outbreak strains. The research addresses the need for effective soap substitutes during viral disease outbreaks, particularly in clinical settings where occupational dermatitis is prevalent. The study finds that Dermol 500 exhibits comparable virucidal activity to alcohol-based hand sanitisers against IAV and SARS-CoV-2, and its components BAK and CD show independent and synergistic virucidal effects. These findings suggest that Dermol 500 could be a suitable alternative to traditional soap substitutes during pandemics. However, the study is limited to in vitro assessments and does not provide clinical data on its effectiveness in real-world settings. The evidence is moderate as it is based on laboratory testing rather than field observations.
